messages:
ana: FYI ran a focused eval on cantare-v1 (int8) and found locale-specific failures for mixed han+latin+rtl snippets. example attached below.
jihoon: paste the sample + tokenizer output?
ana: here: ```
INPUT: "今日 is great — שלום and 漢字!"
TOKENIZER OUT: ["今", "日", " ", "is", " ", "great", " ", "", " ", "ש", "ו", "ל", "ם", " ", "and", " ", "漢", "字", "!"]
EXPECTED: ["今日", " ", "is", " ", "great", " ", "—", " ", "שלום", " ", "and", " ", "漢字", "!"]
```
maya: that stray U+001F/control byte again? we saw similar in the emoji thread last week. did the input sanitizer change for cantare bring-up?
jihoon: no sanitizer change on cantare tokenizer, but we rebased the quant kernel and switched to packed embeddings (shard-aware). small quant shifts + tokenizer ephemeral splits can cause token id distribution differences that cascade in beam search.
eval-bot: run=run-2211, model=cantare-v1-int8, dataset=multilang-mix-rtl, metrics={bleu:-1.12, sacre:-0.95, exact_match_drop:0.08}, anomalies={control_byte_tokens:7, rtl_fragmentation:5, token_id_drift:1.8%}
ana: quick repro: when we force-clean control bytes before tokenization, token merge is fixed and BLEU improves to -0.28. however token_id_drift persists until we revert the packed-embed reorder.
jihoon: OK i'll bisect the quant-pack commits and run a quick delta on token id histograms vs fp16 baseline. if packing reorder is culprit we'll revert or add alignment padding.
maya: let's also add a locale-suite test covering Han+rtl+latin mixtures and a runtime check that logs when a sentence-level token_id histogram KL divergence > 0.02. keep alerting lightweight.
runtime-bot: NOTE: added histogram KL detector metric to nightly pipeline (threshold 0.02). alert channel: #eng-ml-alerts.
jihoon: started bisect: suspect commit 9b2d4f (embed pack reorder). reproduces locally. opening revert PR for canary.
nana: filing a ticket with failing examples and short-term mitigation notes. tagging @support in case customers see this.
summary: cantare-v1 int8 onboarding shows mixed Han+RTL+Latin token fragmentation caused by control bytes + embedding pack reorder. Short-term: pre-token control-byte cleanup and canary revert; Long-term: histogram KL detector, locale-suite test for mixed-script sequences, and alignment padding in packed embeddings.
